'''Hideo Ohno''' ({{langx|ja|大野 英男}}; Hideo Ōno; born 18 December 1954, Tokyo) is a Japanese physicist. He is the 22nd president of [[Tohoku University]], succeeding [[Susumu Satomi]] in April 2018.<ref>[https://www.tohoku.ac.jp/en/news/university_news/hideo_ohno_selected_as_president.html University News - Hideo Ohno selected as president]</ref>

== Biography ==
Ohno received B.S., M.S. and Ph.D. degrees from the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1977, 1979 and 1982. He spent one year as a visiting graduate student at Cornell University in 1979.<ref>[http://www.bureau.tohoku.ac.jp/koho/pub/tdp2008/pdf_e/hideo_ohno.pdf Hideo Ohno profile]</ref> He was a lecturer at the School of Engineering at Hokkaido University from 1982 to 1983, and an associate professor from 1983 to 1994. He was a visiting scientist at IBM T. J. Watson Research Center from 1988 to 1990.

In 1994 Ohno was appointed a professor at [[Tohoku University]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://japanest-nippon.com/en/feature/detail.php?id=21 |title=Hideo Ohno "Development of Ferromagnetic Semiconductors" |access-date=2015-02-04 |archive-date=2019-01-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111055026/https://japanest-nippon.com/en/feature/detail.php?id=21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and a professor at the Research Institute of Electrical Communication (RIEC) from 1995.<ref>[https://www.tohoku.ac.jp/en/research/research_highlights/research_highlight_19.html Feature Highlights - Taking memory for a spin]</ref> In 2004 he became the head of the laboratory of Nanoelectronics and Spintronics at [[Tohoku University]]. From 2010 until March 2018, Ohno served as the director of the Center for Spintronics Integrated Systems. He was tipped as a possible candidate to receive a Nobel Prize in 2011, for his work in spintronics.<ref>[http://www.spintronics-info.com/spintronics-researcher-likely-be-contention-nobel-honors Spintronics researcher likely to be in contention for Nobel honors]</ref> Ohno later in 2021 became an international fellow at the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]] (IVA).

== Awards ==
* 1998 - IBM Japan Science Award
* 2005 - [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]], jointly with Hiroyuki Sakaki for "Studies on Quantum Control of Electrons by Semiconductor Nanostructures and Ferromagnetism"
* 2005 - [[EPS Europhysics Prize]], jointly with [[David Awschalom]] and [[Tomasz Dietl]], for their work on ferromagnetic semiconductors and spintronics
* 2011 - Thomson Reuters Citation Laureate
* 2012 - JSAP Outstanding Achievement Award<ref>[http://www.wpi-aimr.tohoku.ac.jp/en/research/researcher/ohno_h.html Researcher Hideo Ohno] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214214125/http://www.wpi-aimr.tohoku.ac.jp/en/research/researcher/ohno_h.html |date=2019-12-14 }} - Advanced Institute for Materials Research</ref>
* 2012 - [[IEEE David Sarnoff Award]], in recognition of his leadership and contribution in the electronics division of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)<ref>[http://www.jst.go.jp/first/english/en-about-us/ohno-hideo.html Hideo Ohno] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160408203521/http://www.jst.go.jp/first/english/en-about-us/ohno-hideo.html |date=2016-04-08 }} - FIRST Program</ref>
* 2016 - [[Asian Scientist 100]], ''[[Asian Scientist]]''
* 2018 - Clarivate Citation Laureate<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://clarivate.com/hall-of-citation-laureates-2018/ |title=2018 Citation Laureates - Physics |access-date=2019-01-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001142346/https://clarivate.com/hall-of-citation-laureates-2018/ |archive-date=2018-10-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2023 - [[Doctor Honoris Causa]] from the [[University of Warsaw]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.uw.edu.pl/japonski-fizyk-doktorem-honoris-causa-uw/ |title=Japoński fizyk doktorem honoris causa UW | access-date=2023-11-16 }}</ref>
